definitions.explanation: Admitting defeat or yielding to an opponent or difficult situation. Used both in serious military/competitive contexts and in everyday situations where one gives up trying. Composed of 降 (descend, surrender) + 参 (go, come — humble).

examples.japanese: この{暑|あつ}さには{降参|こうさん}した。
{何度|なんど}{挑戦|ちょうせん}しても{解|と}けない{問題|もんだい}に、とうとう{降参|こうさん}した。
examples.english: I finally gave up on the problem that I couldn't solve no matter how many times I tried.

notes:
USAGE:
{降参|こうさん} can express both literal surrender (in battle, competition) and figurative giving up (to heat, difficulty, a persistent person). In casual speech, もう{降参|こうさん}だ！ is a common way to express that one has had enough.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {降参|こうさん}する (to surrender, to give in)
- もう{降参|こうさん}だ (I give up already)
- {降参|こうさん}させる (to make someone give in)
- {暑|あつ}さに{降参|こうさん}する (to be defeated by the heat)
